title: Cutaneous Lymphomas
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026 clinical navigator for Cutaneous Lymphomas (Mycosis Fungoides MF, Sezary Syndrome SS, Primary Cutaneous CD30+ Disorders LyP/pcALCL, and Cutaneous B-Cell Lymphomas). Implements Workup First diagnostic checklists (serial punch biopsies, IHC panel CD3/4/8/30/56, blood Sezary flow cytometry, TCR gene rearrangement clonality), TNMB stage-directed therapies (early MF skin-directed topical steroids / mechlorethamine / phototherapy vs advanced/Sezary systemic Mogamulizumab, Brentuximab vedotin, Bexarotene, Romidepsin, ECP). References StewardMD ONCQIS Standard Protocols. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Cutaneous Lymphomas Version 2.2026 (February 13, 2026).

a.text: TNMB blood (B) classification: B0 is <5 percent atypical circulating lymphocytes with negative TCR clone; B1 is >=5 percent atypical cells without B2 criteria; B2 is Sezary count >=1,000/mcL with clonal TCR rearrangement, or CD4+CD7- >=30 percent, or CD4+CD26- >=30-40 percent of lymphocytes. B2 with erythroderma (T4) defines Sezary syndrome.

b.text: Mogamulizumab (anti-CCR4) is Category 1 preferred for Sezary syndrome and MF with blood involvement (B1/B2). The MAVORIC phase 3 trial versus vorinostat improved progression-free survival, with the greatest benefit in Sezary syndrome and B2 blood disease.

c.text: Brentuximab vedotin (anti-CD30 antibody-drug conjugate) is Category 1 preferred for CD30-expressing MF based on the ALCANZA phase 3 trial versus methotrexate or bexarotene, and is preferred systemic therapy for multifocal primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma.

d.text: Skin-directed therapy is preferred first-line for early-stage MF (IA-IIA) because early disease has excellent disease-specific survival and durable remissions are achievable without systemic toxicity. Systemic therapy is reserved for refractory early disease or advanced stages.

e.text: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, leg type is aggressive with inferior survival versus indolent PCMZL/PCFCL and is treated as systemic DLBCL with R-CHOP with or without involved-field radiation (Category 1). Solitary pcALCL has an excellent prognosis and is managed with excision or local RT 24-30 Gy.

nodes.name: Lymphoma Subtype
nodes.title: Cutaneous lymphoma subtype
nodes.description: Step 1: Clinical Presentation. Select the confirmed clinicopathologic subtype. Each subtype has its own Workup First checklist before TNMB staging and therapy.
bullets: Mycosis Fungoides (MF) / Sezary Syndrome (SS): Mature cutaneous T-cell lymphomas presenting with patches, plaques, tumors, or generalized erythroderma with leukemic blood involvement in SS.

Primary Cutaneous CD30+ Lymphoproliferative Disorders: Lymphomatoid papulosis (LyP, chronic self-healing papulonodules) or primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma (pcALCL, solitary or multifocal nodules/tumors).
Primary Cutaneous B-Cell Lymphomas (CBCL): Indolent PCMZL / PCFCL versus aggressive PCDLBCL, leg type. Histology determines curability and whether anthracycline chemoimmunotherapy is indicated.

Subtype assignment requires expert dermatopathology review correlating skin histology, immunophenotype, TCR or IgH clonality, and clinical behavior; re-biopsy when clinicopathologic discordance exists.

options.label: Mycosis fungoides or Sezary syndrome (mature cutaneous T-cell)
Primary cutaneous CD30+ disorder (LyP or pcALCL)
Primary cutaneous B-cell lymphoma (PCMZL, PCFCL, or PCDLBCL leg type)

nodes.name: MF/SS workup
nodes.title: MF/SS: diagnostic workup and TNMB staging workup
nodes.description: Workup First: complete the high-yield diagnostic checklist establishing skin burden, blood involvement, nodal and visceral stage before any therapy is selected.
bullets: Complete skin exam: measure total Body Surface Area (BSA) affected (<10 percent = T1, >=10 percent = T2); document lesion types (patches, plaques, tumors >=1 cm = T3, generalized erythroderma >=80 percent BSA = T4); record baseline photography and mSWAT-style severity.

Multiple 4-mm punch biopsies from the most indurated or suspicious untreated lesions; avoid recently steroid-treated sites; take serial repeat biopsies when the first sample is nondiagnostic because early MF mimics eczema or psoriasis.
Skin IHC panel: CD2, CD3, CD4, CD5, CD7, CD8, CD20, CD30, CD56; assess epidermotropism with Pautrier microabscesses, loss of CD7/CD26, and CD4:CD8 ratio >10:1; quantify percent CD30+ large cells.
TCR gene rearrangement by PCR (gamma/beta) on skin for clonality; compare the skin clone with the blood clone to establish clonal identity.

Peripheral blood flow cytometry to quantify Sezary cells (CD4+CD7- or CD4+CD26- >=1,000/mcL or >=30-40 percent of lymphocytes = B2; >=5 percent without B2 criteria = B1) plus blood TCR clonality; CBC with differential.
Serum LDH, CBC with differential, CMP; HTLV-1 serology when adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma is in the differential.

Staging imaging: contrast CT neck/chest/abdomen/pelvis or FDG-PET/CT is mandatory for Stage >=IIB cutaneous tumors, erythroderma, palpable adenopathy, elevated LDH, or B2 blood; excisional biopsy of a dominant node (preferred over FNA) with TCR clonality when nodes are palpable.
Bone marrow biopsy only for unexplained cytopenias or aggressive clinical course; pregnancy testing and fertility counseling before systemic therapy in patients of childbearing potential.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed - Proceed to TNMB Staging and Therapy

nodes.name: CD30+ workup
nodes.title: CD30+ disorders: diagnostic workup
nodes.description: Workup First: confirm LyP versus pcALCL histology, quantify CD30, and exclude systemic ALCL before selecting local versus systemic therapy.
bullets: Complete skin exam: measure total BSA affected; document lesion types (self-healing papulonodules in crops suggesting LyP types A-E versus persistent nodules/tumors suggesting pcALCL, including ulceration and solitary versus multifocal distribution).

Multiple 4-mm punch biopsies (or incisional/excisional biopsy for large tumors) from representative lesions; serial re-biopsy of persistent, enlarging, or non-regressing lesions to exclude pcALCL arising in LyP.

Skin IHC panel: CD2, CD3, CD4, CD5, CD7, CD8, CD20, CD30, CD56; quantify percent CD30+ large/atypical cells; ALK testing (pcALCL is ALK-negative); DUSP22/IRF4 rearrangement assessment when available for prognostic correlation.
TCR gene rearrangement by PCR (gamma/beta) on skin for clonality; correlate clone across separate lesions and over time.
Peripheral blood: CBC with differential, flow cytometry for circulating atypical cells, LDH, CMP; blood TCR clonality when leukemic involvement is suspected.

Staging imaging: contrast CT neck/chest/abdomen/pelvis or FDG-PET/CT to exclude systemic ALCL, especially with B symptoms, bulky or rapidly progressive tumors, palpable adenopathy beyond the draining basin, or elevated LDH.
Excisional nodal biopsy (preferred over FNA) for suspicious nodes; bone marrow only for cytopenias or suspected extracutaneous spread.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed - Proceed to TNMB Staging and Therapy

nodes.name: CBCL workup
nodes.title: Cutaneous B-cell lymphoma: diagnostic workup
nodes.description: Workup First: confirm indolent PCMZL/PCFCL versus aggressive PCDLBCL leg type and exclude systemic B-cell lymphoma before selecting local versus R-CHOP therapy.
bullets: Complete skin exam: measure total BSA affected; document lesion types (papules, plaques, nodules, tumors), anatomic distribution (leg involvement raises leg-type suspicion), and solitary versus regional versus generalized pattern.

Punch, incisional, or excisional biopsy deep enough to assess architecture; B-cell IHC panel including CD20, CD79a, PAX5, BCL2, BCL6, MUM1/IRF4, CD10, Ki-67, CD30, and CD56 context markers; expert hematopathology review to separate PCFCL with large-cell morphology (indolent) from PCDLBCL leg type (aggressive).
IgH gene rearrangement by PCR for B-cell clonality; FISH or molecular studies (BCL2/BCL6/MYC) when double-hit or transformed disease is suspected.
Peripheral blood: CBC with differential, LDH, CMP; serum protein electrophoresis when indicated; Borrelia serology for PCMZL in endemic regions.

Staging imaging: contrast CT neck/chest/abdomen/pelvis or FDG-PET/CT (mandatory for suspected leg type, tumors, elevated LDH, or B symptoms) plus bone marrow biopsy to exclude systemic marginal zone, follicular, or diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
Baseline cardiac assessment (ECHO/MUGA), hepatitis B/C and HIV screening before rituximab or anthracycline therapy; pregnancy testing and fertility counseling in patients of childbearing potential.

nodes.name: MF/SS TNMB stage
nodes.title: MF/SS: TNMB stage and blood class
nodes.description: Assign TNMB stage and blood class. Early skin-limited disease takes skin-directed therapy; tumors, erythroderma, nodal/visceral, or B2 disease takes systemic therapy.
bullets: Early stage: IA (T1 <10 percent BSA, N0, B0), IB (T2 >=10 percent BSA patches/plaques, N0, B0), IIA (T1-T2 with N1/N2 reactive nodes, B0). Skin-directed therapy preferred.
Advanced MF: IIB (T3 cutaneous tumors, any N, B0-1), III (T4 erythroderma, B0-1), IVA (N3 effaced nodes or B2 blood), IVB (M1 visceral disease). Systemic therapy indicated.

Sezary syndrome: T4 erythroderma plus B2 clonal blood (Sezary cells >=1,000/mcL with clonal TCR, or CD4+CD7- / CD4+CD26- criteria). Leukemic disease requiring blood-directed systemic therapy, usually ECP-based combinations or mogamulizumab.
Nodal assessment: N1/N2 are clinically abnormal nodes with dermatopathic or early involvement; N3 is effaced nodal architecture. Confirm with excisional biopsy, not FNA alone.
Re-stage skin (BSA, photography, mSWAT-style assessment), blood Sezary count with flow, LDH, and PET/CT response after each treatment phase before switching lines.

options.label: Early stage IA, IB, or IIA (T1-T2 patches/plaques, N0-N2, B0)
Advanced stage IIB (tumors), III (erythroderma B0-1), IVA-B (nodal/visceral)
Sezary syndrome (T4 erythroderma with B2 clonal blood)

nodes.name: CD30+ entity and extent
nodes.title: CD30+ disorder: entity and extent of skin disease
nodes.description: Separate self-healing LyP from pcALCL, then separate solitary/localized pcALCL (local therapy) from multifocal disease (systemic therapy).
bullets: Lymphomatoid papulosis (LyP): chronic recurrent self-healing papulonodules; diagnosis is clinicopathologic (waxing/waning course plus CD30+ histology types A-E). Excellent prognosis with a small lifelong risk of second lymphoma.
pcALCL solitary/localized: single lesion or grouped regional lesions without extracutaneous disease on PET/CT. Managed with local excision or RT alone.
pcALCL multifocal/extensive: scattered lesions across regions or bulky tumors not amenable to local therapy. Requires systemic therapy (brentuximab vedotin or methotrexate).
Exclude systemic ALCL in every case: B symptoms, nodal disease beyond draining basin, visceral lesions, or ALK positivity redirect to systemic ALCL management, not this pathway.

options.label: pcALCL multifocal or extensive skin disease

nodes.name: CBCL entity and extent
nodes.title: CBCL: histology and extent of skin disease
nodes.description: Histology decides intensity: indolent PCMZL/PCFCL takes local therapy or rituximab, while PCDLBCL leg type takes R-CHOP chemoimmunotherapy.
bullets: Indolent localized: PCMZL or PCFCL with solitary or regional lesions and no systemic disease. Curable with local RT or excision.
Indolent generalized: PCMZL or PCFCL with widespread skin lesions not amenable to local therapy. Managed with systemic rituximab, not anthracycline chemotherapy.

Aggressive: PCDLBCL leg type (sheets of large B cells, usually MUM1/BCL2 positive, frequent leg involvement, inferior survival). Treated as systemic DLBCL with R-CHOP with or without involved-field RT (Category 1).

Expert hematopathology review is mandatory before committing to R-CHOP: PCFCL with large-cell morphology can mimic leg type but follows an indolent course and must not receive anthracycline chemotherapy.

nodes.name: Early MF skin-directed therapy
nodes.title: Early-Stage MF (IA-IIA): Skin-Directed Therapy
nodes.description: Skin-directed therapy is preferred first-line for Stage IA-IIA MF. Escalate to systemic therapy only for refractory or progressive disease.
bullets: Topical corticosteroids: potent Class I/II agents (e.g., clobetasol propionate 0.05%) applied to limited patches/plaques with taper to intermittent maintenance; monitor skin atrophy, striae, and adrenal suppression with prolonged use.

Topical mechlorethamine 0.016% gel applied once daily to affected skin; counsel on expected irritant/contact dermatitis (manage with treatment breaks, emollients, topical steroids); avoid eyes, face folds, and genitalia initially.

Phototherapy 2-3 times weekly: narrowband UVB for thin patches (preferred in fair skin and hypopigmented variants) or PUVA (oral 8-methoxypsoralen plus UVA) for thicker plaques; eye protection during PUVA and lifelong skin-cancer surveillance.

Local radiation therapy 8-12 Gy (e.g., 8 Gy in 2 fractions) for refractory solitary plaques or tumors; consider low-dose total skin electron beam (12 Gy TSEBT) for extensive refractory early-stage disease.
Topical retinoids (bexarotene gel) or intralesional corticosteroids for selected refractory limited lesions; avoid systemic chemotherapy for skin-confined early disease.

Reassess every 8-12 weeks with BSA, photography, response criteria, Sezary flow when indicated, and LDH; switch to the advanced/systemic pathway on tumor development, erythroderma, nodal progression, or B1/B2 blood; dermatology follow-up every 3-6 months lifelong.

nodes.name: Advanced MF systemic therapy
nodes.title: Advanced MF (IIB-IV): Systemic Therapy
nodes.description: Systemic therapy for tumors, erythroderma B0-1, nodal, or visceral MF. Prefer blood- and CD30-directed agents with trial consideration at every line.
bullets: Mogamulizumab 1 mg/kg IV weekly for 4 weeks then every 2 weeks for MF with blood involvement (B1/B2; Category 1 preferred, MAVORIC trial); monitor infusion reactions, drug rash, hepatitis, and thyroid function.
Brentuximab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks (up to 16 cycles) for CD30-expressing MF (Category 1 preferred, ALCANZA trial); monitor peripheral neuropathy, neutropenia, and glycemic control.
Bexarotene 300 mg/m2 PO daily with prophylactic fenofibrate and levothyroxine; monitor fasting triglycerides, TSH, CBC, and LFTs; teratogenic, strict contraception required.
HDAC inhibitors: romidepsin 14 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 8, and 15 every 28 days or vorinostat 400 mg PO daily; monitor ECG/QT interval, platelets, nausea, and fatigue.
Refractory or high-burden disease: single-agent gemcitabine or liposomal (pegylated) doxorubicin; avoid prolonged multi-agent chemotherapy given short response durations in CTCL.

Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation for young fit patients with refractory advanced disease achieving response; offer a clinical trial at every line; reassess skin, blood Sezary count, nodes, and PET/CT response every 2-3 cycles.

nodes.name: Sezary syndrome therapy
nodes.title: Sezary Syndrome: Blood-Directed Systemic Therapy
nodes.description: Leukemic erythrodermic disease requires blood-directed therapy, usually ECP-based combinations or mogamulizumab, with intensive supportive skin care.
bullets: Mogamulizumab preferred first systemic therapy for B2 Sezary syndrome (Category 1; greatest MAVORIC benefit in SS and B2 blood disease); same dosing and toxicity monitoring as advanced MF.

Extracorporeal photopheresis (ECP) every 2-4 weeks alone or combined with bexarotene, interferon alfa, or phototherapy for erythrodermic disease; plan durable central venous access and monitor citrate reactions and volume shifts.

Combine ECP with a systemic agent (bexarotene or mogamulizumab) when single-modality response is inadequate; add HDAC inhibitor (romidepsin or vorinostat) or brentuximab vedotin (if CD30+) per advanced MF options for refractory disease.
Monitor blood Sezary count with flow cytometry every 4-8 weeks plus skin BSA, pruritus scores, LDH, and nodal exam; restage with PET/CT for suspected visceral spread.

Supportive care: aggressive emollients and wet wraps, antihistamines and gabapentinoids for pruritus, surveillance for skin superinfection and colonization, fluid/electrolyte and thermoregulation monitoring in erythroderma.
Discuss allogeneic transplantation eligibility early for fit patients; offer a clinical trial at every line; avoid multi-agent chemotherapy outside palliation of rapidly progressive disease.

nodes.name: LyP therapy
nodes.title: Lymphomatoid Papulosis: Observation and Low-Intensity Therapy
nodes.description: LyP is chronic and self-healing. Observe localized disease and reserve low-dose methotrexate or phototherapy for extensive symptomatic cases. No multi-agent chemotherapy.
bullets: Observation for confirmed localized self-healing papulonodules without extracutaneous disease; counsel on the waxing/waning course, expected scarring, and the small lifelong risk of a second lymphoma requiring long-term follow-up.
Topical corticosteroids (or intralesional steroids for bothersome lesions) for symptomatic localized disease; no excision or RT needed for routinely regressing lesions.

Low-dose oral methotrexate 10-25 mg once weekly with folic acid for extensive, frequently relapsing, or cosmetically burdensome disease; monitor CBC, LFTs, creatinine, and pulmonary symptoms with baseline and periodic chest imaging.
Phototherapy (narrowband UVB or PUVA) as an alternative for extensive disease or methotrexate-intolerant patients, with standard phototherapy skin-cancer surveillance.

Never give multi-agent chemotherapy for LyP; re-biopsy persistent, ulcerated, or enlarging lesions to exclude pcALCL or transformed disease; obtain PET/CT for atypical or extracutaneous features; follow every 6-12 months lifelong.

nodes.name: Localized pcALCL therapy
nodes.title: pcALCL Solitary/Localized: Excision or Radiation
nodes.description: Solitary or grouped pcALCL without extracutaneous disease is managed with local therapy alone and carries an excellent prognosis.
nodes.path: Cutaneous Lymphoma / CD30 / pcALCL Local Treatment
bullets: Complete surgical excision with clear margins for solitary lesions amenable to resection; observe after complete excision without adjuvant systemic therapy.
Definitive local radiation therapy 24-30 Gy to the involved field for lesions not resected, with positive margins, or grouped regional disease; salvage persistent disease after excision with RT.
Confirm ALK-negative pcALCL histology and exclude systemic ALCL with PET/CT before committing to local-only therapy; excise and study any draining palpable node.

Counsel on excellent disease-specific survival with frequent cutaneous relapses managed by repeat local therapy; skin surveillance every 3-6 months; re-biopsy new persistent tumors and restage dissemination.

nodes.name: Multifocal pcALCL therapy
nodes.title: pcALCL Multifocal/Extensive: Systemic Therapy
nodes.description: Multifocal skin disease not amenable to local therapy requires systemic treatment, preferring brentuximab vedotin or low-dose methotrexate.
nodes.path: Cutaneous Lymphoma / CD30 / pcALCL Multifocal Treatment
bullets: Brentuximab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks (preferred) for multifocal or extensive pcALCL; monitor peripheral neuropathy, neutropenia, and infusion reactions.
Low-dose methotrexate 10-25 mg PO once weekly with folic acid as an alternative, especially for slower-paced multifocal disease; monitor CBC, LFTs, creatinine, and pulmonary status.
Low-dose involved-field RT for symptomatic bulky lesions alongside systemic therapy; do not use CHOP-type multi-agent chemotherapy for skin-confined multifocal pcALCL.

Restage with skin photography, lesion counts, and PET/CT after 3-4 cycles; biopsy nonresponding lesions to exclude transformed or systemic disease; reserve transplantation and trials for extracutaneous dissemination.

nodes.name: Indolent CBCL local therapy
nodes.title: Indolent CBCL Localized (PCMZL/PCFCL): Radiation or Excision
nodes.description: Localized indolent CBCL is curable with local therapy. Confirm indolent histology and exclude systemic lymphoma first.
nodes.path: Cutaneous Lymphoma / CBCL / Indolent Local Treatment
bullets: Definitive low-dose involved-site radiation therapy for solitary or regional PCMZL/PCFCL lesions (excellent local control); preferred for lesions not easily excised or in cosmetically sensitive areas.
Complete surgical excision with clear margins as an alternative for small solitary lesions; observe completely excised lesions without adjuvant therapy.

Confirm indolent histology (no sheets of large cells, no leg-type immunophenotype) with expert review and exclude systemic marginal zone or follicular lymphoma (CT or PET/CT, marrow when indicated) before local-only management.

Intralesional corticosteroids or intralesional rituximab for cosmetically sensitive or recurrent limited lesions; follow every 3-6 months; re-biopsy rapidly growing lesions with LDH rise to exclude transformation.

nodes.name: Indolent CBCL systemic therapy
nodes.title: Indolent CBCL Generalized (PCMZL/PCFCL): Rituximab
nodes.description: Generalized indolent CBCL is managed with systemic rituximab. Anthracycline chemotherapy is not indicated.
nodes.path: Cutaneous Lymphoma / CBCL / Indolent Generalized Treatment
bullets: Systemic rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV weekly for 4 weeks for generalized PCMZL/PCFCL skin disease; premedicate for infusion reactions and screen for hepatitis B (surface antigen, core antibody) before therapy.
Intralesional rituximab for select symptomatic lesions when systemic therapy is not desired; low-dose involved-site RT to symptomatic fields as an adjunct.
Consider a doxycycline trial for Borrelia-associated PCMZL in endemic regions alongside lymphoma-directed therapy per infectious-disease guidance.
Never give anthracycline-based chemotherapy for indolent CBCL; restage skin (photography, lesion counts) every 8-12 weeks; re-biopsy nonresponding or transforming lesions.

nodes.name: Leg-type CBCL therapy
nodes.title: PCDLBCL Leg Type: R-CHOP With or Without Radiation (Category 1)
nodes.description: Leg-type CBCL is aggressive and treated as systemic DLBCL with R-CHOP chemoimmunotherapy with or without involved-field radiation.
bullets: R-CHOP-21 for 6 cycles (rituximab plus cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisone) with or without involved-field radiation to bulky or residual sites (Category 1); full-dose intensity preserved in fit patients.

Baseline cardiac assessment (ECHO or MUGA), hepatitis B/C and HIV screening, CBC, LDH, CMP, and pregnancy testing before therapy; G-CSF primary prophylaxis per age and comorbidity; antiemetics and tumor-lysis precautions for bulky disease.

Interim and end-of-treatment FDG-PET/CT response assessment by Lugano criteria; biopsy residual PET-avid skin or nodal disease; salvage nonresponders per the systemic DLBCL pathway with clinical trial priority.

Expert hematopathology review is mandatory before cycle 1 to exclude PCFCL with large-cell morphology (indolent, no anthracycline); long-term surveillance for relapse and late anthracycline or RT toxicity.
